key: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
s: Early in a hymn to Agni as a newborn infant, the verse turns to his births; Sāyaṇa, on 1.95.3, reads them as the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning, taking ‘the waters’ as a name for mid-air.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.95.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 333253 (2022)

evidence.words: अस्याग्नेस्त्रीणि जन्मानि संभवन्ति । "समुद्रे अब्धौ वडवानलरूपेण “एकं जन्म । “दिवि द्युलोके आदित्यात्मना “एकम् । "अप्सु । आपः इति अन्तरिक्षनाम । अन्तरिक्षे वैद्युताग्निरूपेणैकम् ।
evidence.gloss: This Agni has three births: in the ocean, one birth, in the form of the submarine (mare’s) fire; in heaven, one, as the sun; in the waters: āpaḥ is a name of mid-air, so in mid-air, one, in the form of the lightning fire.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Problem holds. Re-opened packet.js veda 12 --verse 1.95.3 (revision 333253): Sāyaṇa takes samudre as the ocean (vaḍavānala, submarine fire), divi as the sun, and apsu with āpaḥ iti antarikṣanāma, so the lightning is in mid-air, which is Griffith’s ‘in the waters’, while Griffith’s ‘mid-air’ is Sāyaṇa’s ocean. The old sentence put ‘lightning in mid-air’ against a key that prints mid-air first, so the reader could not match them. CORRECTED to name the mapping from his own gloss: ‘taking ‘the waters’ as a name for mid-air’ (two key words quoted, within rule 3). The seasons clause is dropped, and the evidence trimmed to the births passage, which carries every part of the new reading. Commentator, place, key, src unchanged. verse.js ok (1.95.3, at [94,3]); entry-check ok; 42 words.
